extracted.intended_audience: literary scholars, librarians, editors, and readers using a yearbook/index of short stories
extracted.subtask_description: Conventions and metadata for an index of short stories in books (coverage Oct 1920–Sep 1921), including how distinctions are indicated and how to interpret abbreviated source citations and cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asterisk distinction levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Note. One, two, or three asterisks are prefixed to the titles of stories to indicate distinction. Three asterisks prefixed to a title indicate the more or less permanent literary value of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The index marks titles with one (*), two (**), or three (***) asterisks to signal levels of distinction; three asterisks are explicitly explained as indicating the (approximate) permanent literary value. (The page does not provide explicit textual definitions for one- or two-asterisk levels beyond 'indicate distinction'.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Index coverage period
rubrics_metrics.description: INDEX OF SHORT STORIES IN BOOKS OCTOBER. 1920,:TO SEPTEMBER. 1921
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The index is bounded to works (stories in books) published/collected within the stated period; users should interpret included items as belonging to that date range when using the index.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviation conventions for source works
rubrics_metrics.description: The following abbreviations are used in the index: (e.g.) Aumonier Aumonier. Golden Windmill and Other Stories. Bercovici Bercovici. Ghitza and Other Romances of Gypsy Blood. Brown B Brown. Homespun and Gold. ... (full list of abbreviation→work mappings follows on the page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers must expand the printed abbreviations to the full book titles given in the abbreviations list to interpret the index entries correctly; the page provides a long mapping of short codes (author or short label) to full titles for this purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross references after an author's name refer to previous volumes of this series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an author's name in the index is followed by a cross-reference, that reference points the reader to the author's entries in earlier volumes of the yearbook series; use these cross-references to trace earlier appearances or related listings.
